study_identification_part.si_4_title: Normative modelling of brain morphometry across the lifespan with CentileBrain: algorithm benchmarking and model optimisation

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study collated data from 87 datasets from 20 countries (Europe, Australia, USA, South Africa, and East Asia). Major publicly accessible datasets include: UK Biobank (n=14496), ABCD (n=3116), HCP-YA (n=1113), HCP-A (n=725), HCP-D (n=652), IMAGEN (n=1840), Cam-CAN (n=643), ABIDE-I (n=438), ABIDE-II (n=433), ADHD-200 (n=389), HBN (n=214), GSP (n=2010), MCIC (n=93), NKI-Rockland (n=140), ADNI (n=133). Additional datasets include site-specific samples from various institutions (BIG, BIL&GIN, QTIM, MAS, Betula, NESDA, NTR, etc.). Data was organized through the ENIGMA Lifespan Working Group.

answer.HCP-EP: clinical validation (independent dataset, not included in normative modeling)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The 87 datasets were used for normative model development. Sex-specific subsamples were split into training (80%) and testing (20%) subsets through stratified randomisation by scanning site and age. Two independent datasets (SLIM: n=118; QTAB: n=259) were used to test longitudinal stability of the models over approximately 2 years. The HCP-EP cohort (91 patients with early psychosis and 57 healthy individuals) was used as an independent dataset for clinical validation to test diagnostic classification and symptom severity prediction.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Sex-specific subsamples of the study sample were split into a training subset (80%) and a test subset (20%), through stratified randomisation by scanning site and age." "The Southwest Longitudinal Imaging Multimodal Study (SLIM) and the Queensland Twin Adolescent Brain Study (QTAB) were used to test the longitudinal stability of the optimal normative models. There is no participant overlap between the SLIM and QTAB studies and between either dataset and the sample used for model development."

model-1.model-name: sex-specific MFPR models (150 regional morphometric measures)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative modeling framework was developed using data from 37,407 healthy individuals. Sex-specific models were developed for each of the 150 regional morphometric measures (68 cortical thickness, 68 cortical surface area, 14 subcortical volumes). The sample was split 80/20 for training/testing. Female subsample: 19,964 total (approx. 15,971 training, 3,993 testing). Male subsample: 17,443 total (approx. 13,954 training, 3,489 testing).

The training phase age statistics are not separately reported, but given the stratified randomisation by site and age, they should be similar to the overall values. Age range 3-90 years covers lifespan from early childhood to late adulthood.
